transferTax.stateRateDescription: $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration ($1.10 plus an additional $2.20), levied only when consideration exceeds $100 (Ark. Code § 26-60-105)
transferTax.notes: The tax applies only when consideration exceeds $100, so gifts and no-consideration transfers to a revocable trust owe none. Transfers between a business entity and its member incident to capitalization or reorganization are exempt under 26-60-102(11). Unless otherwise agreed, paid half by seller and half by buyer.

sources.label: Arkansas DFA - Real Property Transfer Tax
sources.quote: The tax rate is $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions that exceed $100.

sources.label: Ark. Code § 26-60-105 (FindLaw)
sources.quote: when the consideration for the lands, tenements, or other realty conveyed exceeds one hundred dollars ($100)

sources.label: Ark. Code § 26-60-102(11) (FindLaw)
sources.quote: An instrument conveying land between corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, or other business entities or between a business entity and its shareholder, partner, or member incident to the organization

propertyTaxAffidavit.formName: Real Property Transfer Tax Affidavit of Compliance
propertyTaxAffidavit.notes: Presented to the county recorder with the deed, with documentary stamps. A clearly exempt instrument can instead carry the statement 'This instrument is exempt from the real property transfer tax'; if no tax is due but the exemption is not clear (for example a no-consideration gift), the affidavit states that fact and is signed by the grantee.

sources.label: Ark. Code § 26-60-107 (FindLaw)
sources.quote: Real Property Transfer Tax Affidavit of Compliance Form

sources.label: Ark. Code § 26-60-110 (FindLaw)
sources.quote: An affidavit or compliance form from the Department of Finance and Administration or a receipt showing proof of tax paid is not required to be attached to an instrument that is exempt from the payment of the real property transfer tax

recording.notes: Uniform county recorder fee under Ark. Code 21-6-306: $15.00 for the first page (one side) and $5.00 for each additional page, so a 1-3 page deed costs $15-$25. Extra $25 if the recorder waives format requirements for good cause.

sources.label: Ark. Code § 21-6-306 (FindLaw)
sources.quote: fifteen dollars ($15.00) for one (1) page, one (1) side only, and five dollars ($5.00) for each additional page
